one_sentence_story: Coined by Joachim Bodamer in 1947, Prosopagnosia ('face blindness') shows that damage or atypical wiring in right fusiform-temporal pathways can erase conscious face recognition while leaving 20/20 eyesight, voice recognition, and even unconscious emotional sweat responses to loved ones intact.
so_what_for_you: If you or a colleague struggle to place faces out of context (~1 in 50 people do!), introduce yourself warmly with your name when meeting outside usual settings ('Hi Sam, it's Jordan from third floor!') — five kind words instantly bridge the fusiform gap.
